result.summary: Mrs Haddad reported a boiler losing pressure and cold radiators. She is the tenant of Flat 4 in the CRM, but she asked for someone to attend Flat 6, which is let to J. Okafor. She then said the boiler is in a shared utility cupboard on her landing. Until we know which flat's boiler it is, we don't know which landlord to ask or where to send an engineer, and there is no contractor or landlord contact on file. I emailed the tenant to confirm the flat and ask about vulnerability, with safety advice, set a 12-hour hold, and escalated at high priority.

judgement.why_this_decision: Event 2 shows the sender is the tenant of Flat 4 and that Flat 6 belongs to someone else. Event 4 says the boiler is in a shared landing cupboard, so the boiler could serve either flat or be communal. That decides who pays and who approves. It is urgent (cold weather forecast, event 3; Jev rated it an emergency), but there is no known vulnerable tenant, no leak or gas risk, no contractor on file and no landlord contact. Sending an engineer now could mean the wrong flat or the wrong person paying.

alternatives_considered.option: Send an engineer as an emergency now
alternatives_considered.why_not: There is no contractor on record, the flat is unconfirmed, no vulnerable tenant is known and there is no gas or water risk. That falls short of the emergency criteria, and it could commit the wrong landlord's money.
The boiler may belong to Flat 6 or be communal. Landlord 2 also has no contact details or preferred channel on file.

alternatives_considered.option: Just ask the tenant and wait
alternatives_considered.why_not: It is urgent and the property details conflict. A person should check building records and phone the tenant today rather than wait for an email reply.
